pool.text: Captain Diego de Losada laid the foundations of the city of Santiago de León de Caracas.
Caracas became the capital of the Spanish Empire's Venezuela Province under governor Juan de Pimentel.
The Central University of Venezuela was founded as the oldest university in the country.
The Guipuzcoan Company of Caracas was founded by the king and cacao business grew.
Luis de Unzaga created the Captaincy General of Venezuela with Caracas as capital.
The successful Venezuelan Declaration of Independence took place following earlier independence efforts in Caracas.
An earthquake destroyed Caracas and disrupted the population before later historical conflicts concluded.
Tributaries of the Guaire River began being used for sewage collection during government leadership.
Caracas became part of the Union of Ibero-American Capital Cities.
A mysterious black substance referred to as La Mancha Negra oozed from roads.
The University City of Caracas designed by Carlos Raúl Villanueva was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
A United Nations survey reported that the cost of living in Caracas was relative to New York.
Caracas had the highest murder rate in the world, surpassing deaths during the Iraq War.
Caracas was designated as the most violent city in the world.
Caracas ranked as the city with the sixth highest homicide rate outside a warzone.
The United States launched strikes on Caracas and captured President Nicolás Maduro and Cilia Flores.
A powerful earthquake doublet struck the city, causing widespread damage, casualties, and injuries.
